sections.markdown:
## C — Testing: knowledge exam, road skills, vision

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
Virginia testing can include a vision screening, a two-part knowledge exam, and a road skills test, and a DMV representative tells each applicant which tests apply [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
You must take the knowledge exam unless you hold a valid driver license from another United States state, Canada, Germany, France, or the Republic of Korea [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
The two-part knowledge exam runs on a computer and covers traffic signs, motor vehicle laws, and safe driving, with every question drawn from this manual [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
Part one holds ten traffic sign questions, and you must answer all ten correctly before part two is allowed [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
Part two is general-knowledge multiple choice, and passing it requires at least 80 percent correct [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
A failing applicant under age 18 must wait a full 15 days before retaking; failing on January 1 means January 17 is the earliest retake [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
Only one attempt is allowed per business day; the exam comes in an audio version and many languages including American Sign Language, so translators are barred where those are offered [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
After three knowledge-exam failures, a fourth attempt requires completing and passing the classroom part of driver education [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
Drivers age 18 or older may instead finish an 8-hour DMV-approved course based on this manual, taken after the third failure at a training school or online, and retake after giving DMV the completion certificate [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
Drivers younger than 18 may use that manual course only after finishing classroom driver education, and must show the classroom certificate to the training school first [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A01
While testing you may not get help, help another person, seek or share questions or answers, or use a cell phone [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A01
A sample knowledge exam appears in Section 8 of this manual and on the DMV website [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A01
Customers with special needs or disabilities should tell DMV staff at any location when they need help with applications or testing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
The road skills test is required unless you hold a valid license from another United States state, Canada, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea, or Taiwan [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
You must supply the test vehicle, which cannot be an autocycle and must show a valid inspection sticker, plates, registration card and decals, plus working brakes, belts, horn, lights, signals, mirrors, and speedometer [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
The examiner requires either an accepted driver-education completion certificate or a completed behind-the-wheel checklist on DMV form CSMA 19, with a licensed driver certifying supervised practice and permit-rule compliance [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
Applicants under 18 take the road skills test inside their driver-education course at a public, private, or commercial school, while home-schooled applicants follow information sheet HS 3 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A02
At 18 or older you must hold the learner permit for 60 days before the first road test or finish approved driver education; the school tests driver-education students while DMV staff test permit holders [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A02
The road test allows one attempt per business day; after a failure you wait two days, and after three DMV failures the fourth attempt waits until you pass the in-vehicle part at an approved school and deliver the certificate to DMV, with that completion dated after the third failure [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
Vision screening means reading letters or numbers in a machine; it is not a medical exam, and failing it can send you to an eye care professional [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
If glasses or contacts are needed to pass screening, you must wear them while driving with a C restriction on the license; after laser surgery the restriction lifts by passing screening unaided at a customer service center or filing Vision Screening Report MED 4 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A02
An unrestricted license needs at least 20/40 vision in one or both eyes plus at least 110 degrees of horizontal vision in one or both eyes, or a comparable field measurement [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A02
Daylight-only driving needs at least 20/70 vision and at least 70 degrees horizontal; with one eye that means 30 degrees or better toward the nose and 40 degrees or better toward the temple, or a comparable measurement [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A02
Daylight-only permission covers only the period from a half-hour after sunrise to a half-hour before sunset [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A02
Drivers wearing bioptic telescopic lenses should read DMV publication MED 44 on licensing information for bioptic lens wearers [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
